steps.question: Do the 6 treated and 6 control muscle samples separate by condition on PCA/MDS of the log2(TPM+1) matrix, and are there outlier samples or unexpected structure not captured in the metadata (12 x 2 sample table)?

grounding.reason: Input is already log2(TPM+1); QC runs on the log values as-is per R-0071, no re-transform, PCA/MDS on top 500 variable genes.

steps.description: Load log_expr.csv (12000 genes x 13 cols, first col likely gene ID) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition). Confirm sample-column alignment between the two files. Since values are already log2(TPM+1), do not re-log-transform. Compute PCA/MDS on the top 500 most-variable genes, a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, and per-sample detected-gene counts (fraction of genes above a low-expression floor), colored by treated/control. Report any sample that fails to cluster with its condition group.

steps.name: Filter, model design, and limma-trend differential expression
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes differ significantly in expression between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) muscle samples?

grounding.reason: Log-normalized input requires: independent mean-log-expression filter (R-0075), no renormalization plus range check (R-0074), explicit reference level and named contrast (R-0036), limma-trend never a count model (R-0019), robust eBayes (R-0093), BH-adjusted selection via topTable (R-0044, R-0043).

steps.description: Filter out genes whose mean log2(TPM+1) across all 12 samples falls below a low floor, or that fail to clear that floor in at least 6 samples (the smaller group size), independent of condition labels. Do not renormalize the values further, but verify the numeric range is consistent with log2 scale (roughly 0-20 with fractional values) before modeling — report the observed range explicitly and flag if it looks like raw counts or unlogged TPM instead. Build a two-level factor for condition with 'control' set as the explicit reference level (do not rely on alphabetical default), fit a limma linear model (design ~ condition) on the filtered log-expression matrix, and moderate variances with eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE). Extract the treated-vs-control contrast via topTable with BH adjustment, reporting log2FC, moderated t, p-value, and adj.P.Val per gene. Select differentially expressed genes at adj.P.Val < 0.05.
acceptance_criteria: Filtering threshold and resulting number of tested genes (of the original 12000) reported
Value-range check performed and stated in output (confirms log2 scale, not raw counts)
Reference level explicitly set to control; contrast named 'treated - control'
limma eBayes called with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE
Full topTable output (all tested genes) saved with logFC, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val
Number of genes at adj.P.Val < 0.05 reported

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on Hallmark and Reactome gene sets
steps.question: Which coordinated biological pathways or processes (MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome) are enriched among genes ranked by their treated-vs-control moderated t-statistic in muscle tissue?

grounding.reason: Ranked GSEA on full list (R-0107, R-0045) using Hallmark then Reactome for human (R-0048, R-0098); Entrez mapping with unmapped-share report (R-0101); 15-500 size window (R-0047); collapse redundant sets (R-0052); ranking metric is a stated disputed choice (R-0108) — moderated t chosen as the Wald-statistic analog since no DESeq2 Wald stat exists for log-normalized limma-trend data.

steps.description: Take the full ranked list of tested genes (all genes surviving the T1S2 filter, not only the significant ones) ranked by the limma moderated t-statistic (used here as the Wald-statistic analog per the disputed ranking-metric rule; state this choice explicitly in output). Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the fraction of unmapped or many-to-many symbols. Run fgsea against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets) as the primary collection, restricting to sets with 15-500 member genes after intersecting with the tested-gene universe. Run a second pass against the Reactome human pathway gene sets as a follow-up collection. Adjust p-values by BH within each collection, collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea::collapsePathways), and report the leading-edge genes for each significant set (padj < 0.05) plus the estimated set size after filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Gene symbol-to-Entrez mapping performed with org.Hs.eg.db; unmapped/multi-mapped share reported
fgsea run on full ranked gene list (not thresholded) against MSigDB Hallmark (50 sets, human)
Second fgsea pass run against Reactome human pathway gene sets
Gene sets restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with tested genes
Ranking metric (moderated t-statistic) explicitly stated as the chosen side of the disputed rule
Redundant significant sets collapsed; leading-edge genes reported per significant set
If a collection is found absent at run time, step reports the gap rather than failing silently

steps.question: What is the final, reproducible summary of differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways between treated and control muscle samples, with all methodological choices documented?

grounding.reason: Report must name method/versions/design/thresholds/counts (R-0041), enrichment DB/version/metric/universe/window (R-0051), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading-edge genes (R-0105), and a full reproducibility record (R-0086).

steps.description: Assemble a report covering: the method (limma-trend on log2(TPM+1) values, no count model used because the facility delivered normalized log values not counts), package versions (limma, fgsea, org.Hs.eg.db) via sessionInfo, the design formula and the named contrast (treated - control, control as reference), the filtering floor and number of genes tested (of the original 12000), the adj.P.Val<0.05 threshold and number of DE genes, the full DE gene table, the GSEA gene-set database names and versions (MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1, Reactome current), the ranking metric used (moderated t-statistic) with the disputed-choice caveat stated, the universe and size window (15-500), leading-edge genes per significant enriched set, and an explicit caveat that enrichment results are method-dependent (a different ranking metric or ORA on the same DE list could give a different set list) and should be read as hypotheses. Also state that only 6 vs 6 unpaired replicates were available and no batch/covariate structure was reported.
acceptance_criteria: Report includes sessionInfo/package versions, design formula, contrast, filtering floor, number of tested and DE genes
Report includes GSEA collection names+versions, ranking metric with disputed-choice note, universe, size window, leading-edge genes per significant set
Report explicitly states enrichment method-dependence caveat
Report states the n=6/6 unpaired, single-batch design limitation

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE (limma-trend) + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The delivered matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) is log2(TPM+1) values from the core facility, not raw counts, so count-based tools (DESeq2/edgeR) do not apply. Following the grounded procedure for log-normalized bulk RNA-seq: (1) QC on the log values to confirm sample structure and detect outliers or batch structure the profile did not flag, (2) a mean-log-expression floor filter independent of the group labels, (3) no renormalization of already-normalized values but an explicit value-range sanity check, (4) an explicit control-as-reference factor releveling so the treated-vs-control contrast direction is unambiguous, (5) a limma-trend linear model (trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE eBayes) — the correct model family for log-scale data with 6 vs 6 unpaired, single-batch replicates, (6) BH-adjusted topTable selection at adj.P.Val<0.05, (7) fgsea preranked GSEA on the moderated t-statistic against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome (both staged locally for human), and (8) a reproducibility-complete report. No batch or covariate structure was reported, so the design is a single two-level factor with no blocking term.
